speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how many hours old the baby was before this bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium started? Also, has the baby had any stool at all since birth, or is the abdomen the only place where we see signs of blockage?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby have a family history of cystic fibrosis, and can you describe the texture of the vomit or the stool that was eventually passed, if any? Also, does the infant seem to be in significant pain or lethargic?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and failure to pass meconium in a newborn, I suspect a distal obstruction like meconium ileus, which is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis. I will request specific imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease. Vital Signs: Heart Rate 145 bpm, Respiratory Rate 40 breaths/min, Temperature 37.5°C (99.5°F). Abdominal Examination: Noticeable distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound indicating gas, firm and distended abdomen with palpable bowel loops and signs of discomfort.
